title: AI Commercial Generator vs Production Company: Which to Hire
summary: An AI commercial generator is software your team runs. An AI commercial production company delivers finished spots. Compare scope, revisions and rights.
body_markdown:
## Which provider fits which kind of commercial?


Provider Model Best fit Published price


Knowlify Done-for-you AI commercials, AI UGC and animation Brand-authored spots for Facebook and Instagram, with human checks From $5,000 a month


Creatify Studio Managed team at a software vendor Teams that want a per-video price from a software company $100 to $200 per video


351 Studio AI video production with human direction Social ads with captions, hooks and revision rounds Not published


Airpost Platform plus dedicated AI video team Ongoing ads uploaded to your Meta account From $6,000 a month


Admiral Media Fixed AI creative batches Game and app advertisers buying batches €10,000 for 20 ads to €29,000 for 80


Higgsfield Marketing Studio generator A team with an operator who regenerates and reviews Plan amounts not shown in our check


AdCreative.ai Ad generation software A team that generates, chooses and downloads its own creatives Not listed in our check


Prices are as of October 2026 and change, so confirm each one on the provider's page. Each row sells a different unit, which is why the next section matters.


## How do you compare quotes that use different units?


Production quotes arrive per video, per month or per batch, and a generator arrives as a plan. Convert each to one unit: an approved commercial of a stated length, in the formats you will upload. Creatify Studio quotes per video, Airpost by the month and Admiral Media by the batch, so a $6,000 monthly plan and a €10,000 batch only compare once you know how many accepted spots each produces.


Ask every provider the same five questions in writing:


- How many scenes and seconds does one finished commercial include?
- How many revision rounds are included, and what counts as a round?
- Which formats and aspect ratios are delivered?
- Who checks the final export, and what do they check?
- Who owns the scripts, the generated presenter and the source files?


Add your own team's hours to a generator's price before comparing. Our[DIY cost comparison](https://knowlify.com/articles/diy-ai-video-ads-vs-done-for-you) shows how to divide total cost by accepted ads. For how the format works scene by scene, read our[AI commercial video production guide](https://knowlify.com/articles/ai-commercial-video-production) .


## When is a generator the better choice?


Choose a generator when your team already has someone who writes scripts, judges product accuracy and has time to rerun a scene. It also suits a first test of the format before you commit to a recurring plan. Keep the first test small, and log every regeneration so you can see the real cost per accepted spot.


A hybrid works too. Your team can generate rough scenes and hand them to a production company for finishing, but name the handoff in the contract. Otherwise both sides may redo the same work, and the original bottleneck stays.


## What do Meta, TikTok and the FTC say about AI commercials?


[Meta's transparency update](https://about.fb.com/news/2025/02/gen-ai-transparency-metas-ads-products/) says it labels ads created or significantly edited with its own generative AI creative features. When those tools add a photorealistic AI-generated person, the label appears next to the Sponsored label. Meta also says it will begin detecting ads made with third-party AI tools, but its post does not say that detection is live yet.


[TikTok's advertising policy](https://ads.tiktok.com/resources/help/article/tiktok-ads-policy-misleading-and-false-content) requires disclosure for fully AI-generated or significantly AI-modified content, and says undisclosed AIGC may be rejected or restricted. Check each platform's current rules before you upload.


Testimonials are a separate question. As of October 2026, the[FTC's testimonial Q&A](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/consumer-reviews-testimonials-rule-questions-answers) says there is no blanket ban on AI avatars in marketing, but an avatar is prohibited when the testimonial it delivers is fake or false. Write AI commercials as brand statements, and keep any customer story tied to a real, approved customer.


## Key takeaways


- A generator suits a team that will own scripting, generation, review and approvals.
- A production company suits a brief that must arrive finished and approved.
- Compare quotes on the same unit: one approved commercial, with its length, revision rounds, formats and rights.
- Keep real customers and live demonstrations on film.
- Plan Meta and TikTok disclosure before the first render.


## FAQ


### Is an AI commercial generator cheaper than a production company?


It can have a lower invoice and a higher total cost. Add the hours your team spends scripting, regenerating, editing and reviewing to the software price, then compare that total with a quote for the same accepted commercials. Count only finished versions that pass your own approval checklist.


### Can an AI commercial feature a real customer?


Not as a fabricated testimonial. The FTC distinguishes fictional dramatization from purported consumer experience, so use a real customer's approved words and account when that experience is the evidence. Film that scene instead of generating it.


### Do AI commercials need a disclosure label?


It depends on the platform. TikTok requires disclosure for fully AI-generated or significantly AI-modified content, and Meta labels some ads made with its generative tools. Check each platform's current rules, and keep the disclosure decision with the final file.


### Can I use a generator and still hire a production company?


Yes. Some teams generate drafts in-house and pay a company to finish and review them. Agree which files you hand over, who fixes errors and who approves the final export, so the work is not done twice.


### What should a production quote include?


Ask for the scene count, length, number of finished versions, revision rounds, delivered formats, usage rights and whether a person checks the final export. Ask separately whether campaign management is included, because some providers agree it as a separate scope.
